ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory risk-rated screening of all directors, shareholders, beneficial owners, and authorized representatives against the South African Financial Intelligence Centre (FIC) list, United Nations Security Council consolidated sanctions list, OFAC SDN list, EU/UK consolidated sanctions lists, and domestic terrorist-financing lists; PEP status must be assessed under FICA section 21E. Screening must be completed before onboarding and repeated at least every 90 days thereafter; any positive match triggers enhanced due diligence and a Suspicious Transaction Report where required.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: CIPC Online Services Portal (BizPortal) - Companies and Intellectual Property Commission, South Africa (www.cipc.co.za)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Company names must be expressed in the Roman alphabet and may use one of South Africa's eleven official languages. If a proposed name contains a word from a non-official language or a non-Roman script, a sworn transliteration or translation into English or Afrikaans must be submitted to CIPC. Names must not be offensive, misleading, or falsely imply governmental or regulated-sector status.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If CIPC rejects a proposed name, the applicant has 60 days from the date of notice to apply for reconsideration under the Promotion of Administrative Justice Act 3 of 2000 (PAJA) by delivering written representations to CIPC. For objections based on confusing similarity with an existing name, the applicant may apply to the Companies Tribunal for a decision under section 12(3) of the Companies Act. If the Tribunal or CIPC remains adverse, judicial review may be filed in the High Court within 180 days of the decision.

incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Companies and Intellectual Property Commission (CIPC), an agency of the Department of Trade, Industry and Competition (the dtic)
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Notice of Incorporation (Form CoR 14.1) together with Memorandum of Incorporation (Form CoR 15.1A for private companies)
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital. A private company must have at least one director and at least one shareholder; shares may be fully or partly paid, and no escrow account arrangement is required for cash or in-kind consideration.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED THAT: (1) The incorporation of the Company under the Companies Act 71 of 2008 and filing of the Notice of Incorporation with the CIPC is approved. (2) The inaugural shareholders subscribe to one hundred ordinary shares fully paid, issued per the Memorandum of Incorporation. (3) The registered office address is adopted as the Company’s legal address and filed with the CIPC. (4) The following appointments are confirmed: Director [Name], Company Secretary [Name], and Chief Financial Officer [Name], each to serve until the next annual general meeting. (5) The officers are authorised to open corporate bank accounts and execute banking resolutions.

step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit a name reservation application (Form CoR 9.1) with the proposed company name in order of preference (up to four). Pay the name reservation fee via CIPC online electronic funds transfer. A reserved name remains valid for six calendar months and may be renewed before expiry. Ensure the name does not conflict with registered trademarks or existing company names.
required_dossiers: Certified identity document of each incorporator
Proof of payment of name reservation fee
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If name is rejected on grounds of undesirability or similarity, submit a new CoR 9.1 with alternative names or file an objection with the CIPC Registrar within 20 business days. The preserved reservation number may be extended once.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Preparation and Submission of Incorporation Documents
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Companies and Intellectual Property Commission (CIPC) – Online Company Registration Module
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the Memorandum of Incorporation (Form CoR 15.1A for private companies) and complete the Notice of Incorporation (Form CoR 14.1). Attach the reserved name number, registered office address, directors' particulars and consents. Submit electronically via CIPC e-Services, attach certified ID copies, and pay the prescribed filing fee (ZAR 175).
required_dossiers: Form CoR 15.1A or draft Memorandum of Incorporation
Certified copies of directors' identity documents
Consent to act as director (s66 Companies Act)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If CIPC issues a query or non-compliance letter, respond through the CIPC 'Permanent in Correspondence' channel within 20 business days, provide corrected documents, and pay a resubmission fee if required. Failure to respond may result in rejection.

step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upon approval, CIPC will issue a Certificate of Incorporation and a registration number (XXXX/XXXXXX/07 for private companies). Verify the certificate and file it with corporate records. The Company acquires juristic personality from the date of certificate issuance.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If certificate is not generated within the SLA, request a status update through the CIPC contact centre or IT system; verify payment and filings; re-submit if a system error occurred.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: South African Revenue Service (SARS), CIPC Beneficial Ownership Register, and commercial banks
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register the company for income tax within 60 days of incorporation using the SARS eFiling portal. Obtain a tax compliance status (SARS tax number). Register for VAT if taxable turnover exceeds R1 million (or voluntarily if threshold met). File the initial beneficial ownership declaration with CIPC within 30 days (where applicable). Open a corporate bank account with board resolution and signed mandate.
required_dossiers: Directors' identity documents and residential addresses
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If SARS registration is delayed, contact the SARS branch with proof of submission. For CIPC beneficial ownership queries, respond within 20 days with corrected forms.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: South African Revenue Service (SARS); all national tax registration, filing, and compliance administration is conducted through the SARS eFiling portal (www.sarsefiling.co.za), which is the sole digital gateway for income tax, VAT, customs, and excise matters, with integrated data exchange from the Companies and Intellectual Property Commission (CIPC).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A newly incorporated (Pty) Ltd first obtains its CIPC enterprise registration from the Companies and Intellectual Property Commission; SARS then automatically activates the income tax reference number once the entity has a filing obligation. A non-resident company deriving South African-source income must apply directly to SARS for income tax registration via eFiling and must appoint a resident public officer within 14 days of incorporation or commencement of business activity. Where the entity makes taxable supplies, Form VAT 101 must be lodged through eFiling for VAT vendor registration. Non-resident suppliers of electronic services, including UI/UX design subscription platforms, must use the dedicated foreign electronic-services VAT registration route and will be issued a VAT number commencing with the digit 4, with no requirement of a South African place of business. Upon acceptance, the entity receives its registration confirmation in eFiling and must thereafter maintain its compliance profile, including VAT 201 periodic returns, annual income tax returns, and export record submissions.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: South Africa does not operate a US-style check-the-box regime; a (Pty) Ltd is mandatorily taxed as a company at entity level and cannot elect pass-through treatment. The material statutory elections available are: (1) voluntary VAT registration once taxable supplies exceed R50,000 but remain below the R1,000,000 compulsory threshold; (2) election among approved VAT input-tax apportionment methods under section 17(1) of the VAT Act, with SARS approval required for any special method; (3) election to zero-rate exported services under section 11(2)(l) of the VAT Act, subject to full documentary and substantive compliance; (4) VAT group registration election under section 54 of the VAT Act for related entities with at least 70% ownership; and (5) mandatory, non-elective application of the hybrid mismatch rules under the Income Tax Act and VAT Act, which neutralize double-deduction or deduction-without-inclusion outcomes for cross-border arrangements.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value-Added Tax (VAT) levied under the Value-Added Tax Act 89 of 1991
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: R1,000,000 (South African Rand) per 12-month period is the compulsory VAT vendor registration threshold for taxable supplies, with voluntary registration available from R50,000; however, foreign suppliers of electronic services, including subscription-based UI/UX design services, are subject to compulsory VAT registration with no minimum turnover threshold under the electronic-services rules, applying the payments-based place-of-supply approach now in force.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: SARS does not currently impose mandatory real-time fiscal clearance, continuous transaction control, or digital stamping for VAT invoices. Electronic tax invoices are expressly permitted under section 20(7A) of the VAT Act and must be issued no later than 21 days after the supply. Compliance is structurally driven by eFiling-based VAT 201 declarations, modernised SARS application programming interfaces (APIs), third-party data matching from payment rails such as Stripe and Wise, and risk-based refund verification. SARS has announced an intended evolution toward structured, SAF-T-aligned e-invoicing, but no binding real-time fiscal clearance or API stamping regime applies as at the date of this dossier.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Goods are zero-rated under section 11(1)(a) of the VAT Act where a vendor supplies goods that are exported outside South Africa within 90 days of the date of supply, supported by prescribed export documentation. Services are zero-rated under section 11(2)(l) where the services are supplied to a non-resident who is outside South Africa at the time of supply, the services are not supplied directly in connection with land or movable property situated in South Africa, and the supplier has no reason to believe the services are consumed in South Africa. Remote UI/UX design subscription services delivered to non-resident enterprise clients therefore qualify for the 0% export VAT rate, whereas the same digital subscription supplied to a South African resident attracts 15% VAT under the electronic-services place-of-supply rules. Pure digital service exports do not require a customs declaration, but the vendor must retain complete contracts, subscriber records, IP-geolocation logs, payment settlement evidence, and non-resident status documentation.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: SAD500 Customs Export Declaration lodged electronically via SARS Customs for any physical export consignment
Bill of Lading, Air Waybill, or multimodal transport document evidencing physical cross-border exportation for goods
Foreign Inward Remittance Certificate (FIRC) or regulated-bank SWIFT advice confirming hard-currency settlement of the exported supply
Commercial invoice and design-subscription contract identifying the non-resident counterparty, payment terms, and place of performance
Digital-delivery and usage records, including platform logs, IP-geolocation reports, and subscriber master files, substantiating offshore consumption of UI/UX design services
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Zero-rating claims are subject to strict SARS verification and audit. If the documentary conditions, the 90-day goods-export requirement, or the section 11(2)(l) non-resident use-and-enjoyment conditions are not satisfied, SARS will claw back the zero-rated output as 15% VAT, together with interest at the adjusted prescribed rate. The Tax Administration Act 28 of 2011 understatement penalty framework applies at 0% to 150% of the tax shortfall, scaled to the conduct category from substantial understatement through gross negligence to intentional tax evasion. A fraudulent VAT refund claim attracts additional tax of up to 200% of the refund under section 40(2) of the VAT Act, and deliberate evasion or false export declarations may found criminal prosecution, personal liability of directors, and the imposition of director-level joint and several liability where the conduct is reckless or fraudulent. SARS refund audits generally reach back the applicable five-year prescription period and may withhold refunds pending full verification.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: South African Reserve Bank (SARB) acting through the Financial Surveillance Department (FinSurv) as the Exchange Control Authority under the Currency and Exchanges Act, Act 9 of 1933, and the Exchange Control Regulations, in coordination with the National Treasury and the Financial Intelligence Centre (FIC).
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: ZAR is freely convertible at a market-determined floating rate, with no surrender or conversion ratio for exporters since the 1995 deregulation of the exchange-control system. Current-account payments (dividends, management fees, royalties, service fees) are permitted without prior FinSurv approval provided they are supported by audited after-tax profit certification, SARS tax clearance and standard Balance of Payments (BOP) disclosures. Capital-account inflows (non-resident share subscription) are permitted through an Authorised Dealer without prior FinSurv approval for an ordinary private company; capital repatriation on liquidation is allowed upon proof that the original inflow was recorded on the BOP statement. Practical hurdles for a foreign-owned (Pty) Ltd include strict documentary chains linking inbound funds to the CIPC share register, the 180-day export-proceeds repatriation obligation for service revenue, and the requirement to quote BOP purpose codes on every cross-border wire to prevent misclassification as capital flight.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Service exporters, including digital design subscription agencies, must cause the full value of exported services to be received and repatriated into South Africa within 180 days from the invoice date. There is no mandatory conversion ratio: the exporter may elect either to (a) convert the foreign currency to ZAR immediately through an Authorised Dealer or (b) retain the proceeds in a Foreign Currency Account (FCA), with disposal and recredits subject to the same 180-day rule and periodic reporting to the Authorised Dealer. Each receipt must be reported on the BOP/CFS declaration within 30 days of credit, and underlying service invoices and platform settlement statements (Stripe/Wise aggregated payouts) must demonstrate a clean reconciliation to exports of services to avoid deemed-interest or unexplained-credit scrutiny.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Medium feasibility with material legal constraints. Wise operates in South Africa as a registered accountable institution and licensed financial services provider through a partnership with a local Authorised Dealer bank; it can facilitate inbound USD collections and international payouts but cannot act as a bank for ZAR, and all ZAR settlement must traverse the partner bank's local clearing rails. Stripe operates as a payment facilitator via local acquiring partners and settles USD/EUR via SWIFT into a local Foreign Currency Account; it is not licensed as an EMI by SARB. Offshore digital EMIs (Revolut Business, Payoneer and similar) cannot open ZAR-denominated accounts for South African corporates without a local bank licence, FSP licence and FinSurv registration; their use is limited to holding non-ZAR funds offshore, which creates an immediate 180-day repatriation exposure for the underlying service-export revenue. Recommended architecture: a local tier-1 operational account paired with Wise and Stripe for card and payout collection, with automatic conversion and same-day SWIFT settlement into the local FCA.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Under FICA (Financial Intelligence Centre Act 38 of 2001, as amended) remote onboarding is not statutorily prohibited for low-risk private companies, provided electronic verification is performed against the CIPC registry, the Department of Home Affairs movement-control system for non-resident passport holders, and independent biometric checks. In practice, tier-1 banks require at least one natural-person director or authorised signatory to attend an in-person or high-grade video-call KYC interview; non-resident directors are additionally required to provide a notarised or apostilled passport copy, proof of residential address, and original or notarised board resolutions confirming the signatory mandate. Core documentation: CIPC certificate of incorporation, Memorandum of Incorporation, beneficial-ownership register filed under the Companies Amendment Act 2024, SARS tax clearance certificate, 12-month projected cash flows, and source-of-funds evidence for non-resident shareholders.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Offshore parent or greater than 25% non-resident beneficial ownership structure with complex intermediary holding layers.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Corporate organogram; CIPC beneficial-ownership register extract; apostilled certificates of incorporation for each shareholder; trust deed or declaration of trust where applicable; UBO identity documents and source-of-funds statement; audited or sworn financial statements of the investing entity; reference letters from the remitting foreign bank.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-volume inbound subscription revenue from multiple foreign clients via aggregators (Stripe/Wise) without a local physical office or payroll.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: SARS income-tax registration and tax-clearance certificate; VAT 240 registration or proof of exempt status if below the threshold; executed client subscription agreements and monthly invoice log; platform settlement reports matched to the accounts-receivable ledger; evidence of delivered UI/UX deliverables (project files, design-tool access logs); BOP export-of-services declaration filed through the Authorised Dealer.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Large early-stage share-premium injection from a non-resident investor into a services company with minimal tangible assets.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Share subscription agreement; board resolution allotting shares under Companies Act s.38; CIPC share-allotment notice; source-of-funds documentation (investor bank statements, salary or bonus records, sale-of-asset contracts); authorisation from the investor's home exchange-control authority where applicable; confirmation that the remittance is equity and not a loan to avoid thin-capitalisation or disguised-financing refusal.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Recurring outbound payments to foreign design subcontractors or related parties creating disguised-dividend or transfer-pricing risk.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Master service agreements with daily or hourly rate benchmarks; OECD-style transfer-pricing local file or benchmarking study on comparable service rates; evidence of actual deliverables (Git commit logs, design-export trails, time-tracking reports); SARS advance-pricing agreement where applicable; per-payment MT103 confirmations quoting service purpose codes; employee-versus-contractor classification records demonstrating PAYE/UIF/SDL compliance.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Non-resident shareholders remit via SWIFT MT103 (USD or EUR) to the company's Capital Escrow / Share Subscription account held at the Authorised Dealer, quoting the BOP purpose code for equity participation in a private non-financial corporation (foreign direct investment). The Authorised Dealer issues a BOP cover-note reference at conversion, applies the market rate, and credits the ZAR escrow; the allotment must be reflected in the CIPC share register within 30 days and matched to the board-resolution file. Prior FinSurv approval is not required for ordinary shares in an unlisted private company, but the bank retains the full subscription file (resolution, instrument of subscription, shareholder list, source-of-funds evidence) for a five-year audit trail. Inbound funds without a valid purpose code or with a mismatch to the FICA profile are held in suspense and are not available for disbursement.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: International supplier and subscription-tool payments (Adobe, Figma, AWS, OpenAI, GitHub): SWIFT MT103 from the ZAR operating account via the Authorised Dealer, quoting the current-account services purpose code, with optional conversion under a Forward Exchange Contract. Domestic disbursements (payroll, freelancers, hosting, local SaaS): BankservAfrica Automated Clearing Bureau (EFT/ACH) same-day or next-day rails, or SAMOS (South African Multiple Option Settlement) for urgent high-value ZAR transfers. Commercial Letters of Credit (MT700) are required only where a supplier demands documentary protection; standard practice for SaaS and digital-tool procurement is open-account MT103 settlement against invoice. Platform payouts: Stripe and Wise batch-settle USD/EUR in a single SWIFT MT103 into the company's Foreign Currency Account, after which the treasury desk converts to ZAR; each inbound platform settlement must be reconciled to the individual customer ledger to satisfy the 180-day service-export reporting obligation.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable Forward Exchange Contract (FEC) on USD/ZAR or EUR/ZAR with an Authorised Dealer, covering committed subscription-receivable or supplier-payable exposures for up to 12 months with standard rollover provisions.
Plain-vanilla foreign-currency options (purchased USD put / ZAR call and USD call / ZAR put) acquired from an Authorised Dealer for hedging current-account cash flows without speculative intent.
Foreign Currency Account (FCA) natural hedge, retaining export proceeds in USD or EUR for up to 180 days as a non-derivative warehousing technique, then converting under a rolling FEC.
Cross-currency interest rate swaps (CCIRS) solely to hedge confirmed foreign-currency borrowings or deposits, subject to FinSurv reporting; not available for speculative positions.

Onshore deliverable ZAR forwards only; offshore non-deliverable forwards referencing ZAR are not permissible for resident corporate hedging and must be avoided to prevent exchange-control contravention.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: CIPC Annual Return (Companies Act 71 of 2008, s82) including Beneficial Ownership Declaration
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Companies and Intellectual Property Commission (CIPC), South Africa
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 30 business days after each annual anniversary of incorporation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: CIPC late-filing penalty accrues after the 30-business-day period; two consecutive years of non-filing permit CIPC administrative strike-off/deregistration under s83 of the Companies Act.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Financial Statements (AFS) and auditor's or independent reviewer's report, where the statutory filing obligation applies
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: CIPC via the e-Services filing portal
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: AFS must be approved and presented within 6 months after financial year-end; where a filing obligation exists, file with CIPC within 30 business days after presentation to shareholders
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late or non-filing of required AFS is a Companies Act offence; directors may be subject to administrative fines and the company may be referred to CIPC deregistration procedures.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Beneficial Ownership Register Update / Annual Beneficial Ownership Confirmation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 5 business days of any shareholding transfer or change in beneficial ownership; annual reconfirmation submitted with the CIPC Annual Return
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: CIPC may reject the annual return until the beneficial ownership declaration is filed; failure to file beneficial ownership information constitutes statutory non-compliance carrying administrative penalties and eventual deregistration risk.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory independent IRBA audit is triggered when a company's public interest score is 350 or greater; a public interest score of 100 to 349 requires independent review unless shareholders resolve to audit; public companies, state-owned companies and companies controlling state-owned companies are always subject to audit.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS for public/state-owned companies and publicly accountable entities; IFRS for SMEs for private (Pty) Ltd companies not subject to an audit obligation and not publicly accountable, under the Companies Act 71 of 2008.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The company must maintain an accurate beneficial ownership register at its registered office. Any shareholding transfer or change in beneficial ownership must be lodged with CIPC within 5 business days. The CIPC Annual Return contains an annual beneficial ownership declaration; directors must confirm the register is current and disclose all transfers occurring in the preceding year before the annual return is accepted.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of share certificates and share transfers
Register of debentures and options, if applicable

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 200 - 600 per annum for registered office and company secretarial support
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 4,000 - 12,000 per annum for a statutory audit or independent review engagement when required

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 27% for years of assessment ending on or after 31 March 2023
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No blanket tax holiday. Preferential effective rates arise through statutory deductions: 150% R&D allowance for qualifying technological development under s11D, accelerated capital allowances for qualifying renewable-energy and manufacturing assets under s12B/s12C, industrial policy project allowances under s12I, and the small business corporation graduated tax brackets if the Pty Ltd meets the statutory gross-income and shareholder-ownership tests.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: SARS eFiling: ITR14 Company Income Tax Return
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: The ITR14 must be submitted within 12 months after the end of the company's year of assessment unless SARS prescribes an earlier date by notice. For a standard 28/29 February year-end, this is effectively the last business day of the following February.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Registered legal name, company registration number, SARS tax reference number, financial year-end date, and registered office or postal address.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A non-resident company uses ITR14 only for a South African branch or permanent establishment and must disclose the local representative and branch registration details.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: All amounts received or accrued in respect of UI/UX design subscription services, excluding VAT and amounts collected on behalf of third parties.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A non-resident branch includes only South African-source service revenue attributable to the local permanent establishment and excludes head-office foreign turnover.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Operating expenses incurred in the production of income: salaries, subcontractor fees, software licenses, hosting, marketing, bank charges, rent, and qualifying capital allowances.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Deduct only expenses directly connected with the South African trade; head-office overhead is deductible only when supported by a reasonable allocation and arm's-length transfer pricing.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Brought-forward assessed losses used to reduce taxable income, subject to the 80% taxable-income set-off ceiling applicable to years of assessment commencing on or after 1 April 2023.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Only losses sustained in the South African branch trade may be offset against that branch's taxable income.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Taxable income and normal tax calculation
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable income multiplied by the applicable corporate income tax rate of 27%, before rebates and credits.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A non-resident branch is taxed at 27% on South African-source taxable income only; worldwide income is not aggregated.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Credits and withholding tax relief field
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Foreign tax credits under s6quat, dividend/interest/royalty withholding tax credits, provisional tax payments, and other credits used to discharge the final assessed liability.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A non-resident branch claims treaty relief in accordance with the applicable double taxation agreement and only for South African taxes imposed on the branch's income.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Failure to file ITR14 by the due date triggers an automatic administrative non-compliance penalty: a monthly, turnover-band based penalty up to ZAR 16,000 per month for large companies, capped at 12 months, plus prescribed-rate compounded daily interest. A late, incorrect, or intentionally false return may also attract an understatement penalty of up to 125% of the tax shortfall.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: SARS eFiling: IRP6 Provisional Tax Return
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Twice per year (mandatory provisional estimates), with an optional third top-up after year-end; final reconciliation is made in the annual ITR14.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: First provisional return and payment are due within six months after the start of the year of assessment; the second is due on the last business day of the year of assessment; the optional third top-up is due no later than six months after the year of assessment.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: The lower of the latest assessed taxable income or a revised prudent estimate, used to calculate the first provisional payment.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A non-resident branch uses its South African branch taxable income as reflected in local records, not the worldwide group profit.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Estimated taxable income for the current year
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: A full-year estimate of taxable income from design subscriptions, maintenance fees, consulting and ancillary digital design services.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Include only income attributable to the South African permanent establishment; exclude foreign-source income not subject to South African net income tax.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Section 6quat foreign tax credits and treaty credits available against the provisional normal tax estimate.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A non-resident branch may credit only taxes imposed by its residence country where the applicable DTA preserves South Africa's taxing right and grants a corresponding credit.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Payment of at least 50% of estimated normal tax at each mandatory provisional date; election of the third top-up to reduce potential interest and underestimation exposure.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: No special administrative relief: the same provisional percentages apply to the branch's estimated South African tax liability.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Non-submission or late submission of IRP6 attracts the same monthly administrative penalty as ITR14. Underestimation of provisional tax may trigger a 20% statutory underestimation penalty on the shortfall plus prescribed-rate compound interest until the underlying tax is paid.
